+# Northstar access-request intake
+
+A Python CLI prepares a durable review queue from JSON message exports. PostgreSQL supports shared regional operators and worker processes; SQLite supports single-host development. Intake returns immediately. Workers process documents independently, and operators can inspect completed results while other messages remain pending. Every successful intake awaits human review.
+
+## Setup and reproducible examples
+
+Supported runtime: Python 3.12 (verified on 3.12.3), PostgreSQL 16, and `uv` for locked dependencies. Run from the repository root after installing Python and uv through your normal tooling:
+
+```sh
+uv sync --locked
+uv run python -m intake --help
+uv run python -m intake init
+uv run python -m intake intake materials/requests --provider mock
+uv run python -m intake work --workers 4 --drain
+uv run python -m intake queue
+uv run python -m intake export deliverables
+```
+
+uv.lock pins runtime and development dependencies. The package runs directly from this checkout. The default database is sqlite:///intake.db. The deterministic mock replays reviewed fixtures keyed by decoded message SHA-256; it is not a general extractor. Unknown messages fail explicitly. Example response_source is mock. The source_sha256 is separately computed from original file bytes.
+
+Regenerate all example reports from a fresh database, including the authored paraphrase evaluation:
+
+```sh
+uv run python -m intake.demo
+uv run python -m intake.evaluate .artifacts/accuracy/extractions.jsonl
+```
+
+The demo exports the 20 supplied documents to deliverables. Its separate .artifacts/accuracy/ export includes those plus fixtures/synthetic/SYN-001.json. The evaluator requires all 21 expected documents; evaluating the 20-message deliverable intentionally reports the missing paraphrase. Generated attempt IDs/timestamps vary; facts, routes, hashes and configuration versions are the intended comparisons.
+
+## Shared database and live provider
+
+Provision a PostgreSQL 16 database reachable from the operator hosts. Grant the role access to its dedicated database/schema and configure credentials/TLS through your deployment. All operators use the same DATABASE_URL. Initialize once before starting concurrent operators:
+
+```sh
+export DATABASE_URL='postgresql+psycopg://[REDACTED_EMAIL]/northstar?sslmode=require'
+uv run python -m intake init
+```
+
+The real provider uses OpenAI HTTPS Responses at https://api.openai.com/v1/responses and strict JSON-schema output. The default supported model is gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18. The facilitator provides API_KEY in the environment. Only live workers need the key; keep its value out of source, shell history and logs. OPENAI_MODEL can select another model supporting the same request configuration.
+
+```sh
+uv run python -m intake intake materials/requests --provider openai
+uv run python -m intake work --workers 4
+```
+
+In another terminal with the same DATABASE_URL:
+
+```sh
+uv run python -m intake queue --state queued
+uv run python -m intake queue --state running
+uv run python -m intake queue --state complete
+uv run python -m intake queue --state error
+uv run python -m intake history IT-001.json
+uv run python -m intake export /tmp/northstar-current
+```
+
+Use work --drain for a finite batch; otherwise workers poll for future intake. Graceful Ctrl-C stops new claims and lets in-flight calls finish. Forced termination leaves recoverable leases. queue shows state, available_at (retry time), lease_until (expiry), errors, extraction, version IDs and routing; times are Unix seconds. history includes prior successes and execution events. Processing state complete means extraction finished, while review status remains review or needs-information.
+
+| Environment variable | Use | Default |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| DATABASE_URL | Shared PostgreSQL or single-host SQLite URL; --db overrides | sqlite:///intake.db |
+| API_KEY | OpenAI bearer credential in live worker environment | none |
+| OPENAI_MODEL | Model for intake --provider openai; --model overrides | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 |
+| TEST_DATABASE_URL | Dedicated PostgreSQL database for integration tests | temporary SQLite files |
+
+These are the only variables read by the application/tests. No live provider call was made for this submission. deliverables/request-evidence.json is an illustrative redacted request. Request construction and refusal/incomplete handling follow [official OpenAI Structured Outputs documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses). Account access and factual quality need separate live validation.
+
+## Retries, recovery and input updates
+
+```sh
+uv run python -m intake recover
+uv run python -m intake queue --state error
+uv run python -m intake retry IT-001.json
+uv run python -m intake retry all-errors
+uv run python -m intake work --drain
+```
+
+recover marks claims past their 180-second expiry as visible lease-expired errors. Retry creates a new attempt with the recorded source/configuration. Concurrent retries reuse an existing queued/running attempt. Unchanged intake reuses the current attempt even if it failed: use retry explicitly. Re-intake instead when source or settings have changed. A batch's absent documents remain current.
+
+Each filename is one document, even if multiple documents mention the same request ID. Reusing a filename creates a revision. Original bytes and distinct hashes are retained in source_versions. Attempts/events preserve execution history, and the unique document row points to one current attempt. Queue records include document_id, source_sha256, version_id and attempt_id, matching the extraction record. A failed current attempt shows null extraction and an actionable error; older successes remain in history. A worker completing an older version cannot replace the current pointer.
+
+Fingerprints record source hash, provider/model/configuration, prompt, schema, extraction-policy text, provider implementation, routing implementation and policy hashes. Changed source/model/prompt/schema/extraction policy creates a new extraction. A routing-only change revalidates and reroutes the current valid extraction without a model call, recording reused_from. Policy changes still require implementing/testing the corresponding routing code; prose edits cannot implement arbitrary rules. Failed extractions cannot be reused. Workers reject mismatched provider/routing code. Deploy a consistent checkout and re-intake affected sources. Prompt/schema/configuration snapshots are stored with attempts.
+
+## Operating assumptions and limits
+
+PostgreSQL transaction advisory locks serialize short mutations, with database constraints, row locks and token-fenced leases. SQLite uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Model calls execute outside transactions. Four durable database slots cap concurrent claims across all workers sharing the database. SQLite must remain on one host/local disk; use PostgreSQL for multi-host operations. Access uses controlled shell/service accounts and database permissions; the CLI adds no HTTP server or authentication layer.
+
+Live calls start at least one second apart across the database (at most 60/minute). Attempts make at most three calls. HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504 and network timeouts get persisted exponential delay plus jitter and a shared cooldown. Retry-After seconds/HTTP dates are honored up to one hour; longer cooldowns fail for operator follow-up. Refusals, incomplete/malformed/schema-invalid output, input errors and other HTTP errors fail without automatic retry. Restart retains delays and counts. Quotas shared with other internal tools remain unknown; coordinate account limits and lower CALL_SPACING's resulting rate in intake/store.py if necessary. Deploy identical code/constants on every worker.
+
+Requests use temperature 0, max_output_tokens 2500, store=false and a 30-second socket timeout. A trickling socket can last longer; expired claims cannot publish, but old network calls can overlap replacement work after lease expiry. Calls are at-least-once after interruption; provider billing cannot be exactly-once. No total wall-clock deadline is supplied. The prompt, exact evidence validation and recognizable-override detector reduce risk, but a model can miss novel conflicts or attacks. Human approval remains external. Mock supporting_quotes use the full decoded message as exact source evidence.
+
+At 60 starts/minute, 400 one-call messages take at least about seven minutes and 2,000 about 34 minutes, before latency, quotas/retries. These are calculations, not measured throughput; four slots also constrain throughput at high latency. No 2,000-message soak, regional outage/backup restore or live quality test was run. Operations must manage backups, retention and worker supervision. There is no migration framework or automatic pruning. Database views are live; JSON exports are point-in-time. Both export files derive from one SELECT; after a file-write interruption verify matching attempt IDs and rerun export. Use a separate export directory per operator.
+
+## Verification and capture
+
+```sh
+uv run python -m pytest -q
+uv run ruff check .
+uv run python -m compileall -q intake tests
+# Optionally set TEST_DATABASE_URL to a reachable dedicated PostgreSQL 16 database.
+uv run python -m pytest -q
+```
+
+PostgreSQL tests create/remove uniquely named test schemas. See [verification results](deliverables/verification.md) and [independent accuracy expectations](deliverables/accuracy.md). Mock tests use no provider credential and include a separate process inspecting persisted unfinished work.
+
+Entire is enabled through the existing Codex hooks. The current session was detected using entire session current --json (resolution caller-env). Commits automatically checkpoint sessions; capture and push results are checked at submission time. Submit the root repository URL through Classroom; the application does not submit Classroom forms.

"""Rebuild mock artifacts and the independent accuracy comparison."""

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

from .domain import ROOT, settings
from .evaluate import ROUTES, compare, expected
from .providers import ENDPOINT, request_body
from .store import Store


def main():
    output = ROOT / "deliverables"
    output.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    config = settings()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="northstar-demo-") as temp:
        url = f"sqlite:///{temp}/demo.db"
        store = Store(url)
        store.initialize()
        for path in sorted((ROOT / "materials/requests").glob("*.json")):
            store.intake(path, config)
        while job := store.claim():
            store.process(job)
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "intake", "--db", url, "export", str(output)], check=True)
        assert len(store.view()) == 20
        store.intake(ROOT / "fixtures/synthetic/SYN-001.json", config)
        store.process(store.claim())
        accuracy_dir = ROOT / ".artifacts/accuracy"
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "intake", "--db", url, "export", str(accuracy_dir)], check=True)
        result = compare(store.view())
        assert not result["failures"] and not result["unexpected_documents"], result
        store.engine.dispose()
    (output / "accuracy-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    request_config = settings("openai")
    example = json.loads((ROOT / "materials/requests/IT-001.json").read_text())
    evidence = {
        "observation": "Illustrative implemented request; no live provider call was made.",
        "method": "POST", "url": ENDPOINT,
        "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <REDACTED>", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        "body": request_body(request_config, "IT-001.json", example["message"]),
        "timeout_seconds": 30, "maximum_calls_per_attempt": 3,
        "response_handling": {
            "implementation": ["intake/providers.py:parse_response", "intake/domain.py:validate",
                               "intake/store.py:process", "intake/store.py:finish"],
            "success": "Require completed response and message, no error/refusal, exactly one JSON text; validate snapshot.schema.json, ISO dates and source quote/fact coverage before routing.",
            "failure": "Null extraction; error / IT Service Desk / retry-extraction. Do not log provider body or exception text.",
            "transient": "HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504 and network timeouts: durable delayed retries, at most 3 calls; shared cooldown and jitter. Refusal, incomplete and malformed output fail without automatic retry.",
            "retry_after": "Honor seconds or HTTP-date up to 3600s; larger cooldown fails for operator follow-up.",
        },
    }
    (output / "request-evidence.json").write_text(json.dumps(evidence, indent=2) + "\n")
    lines = [
        "# Source-grounded comparison (mock replay)", "",
        "Expected facts in tests/expected.tsv were authored directly from the decoded source messages and office policy, separately from fixtures/mock-responses.json. Agreement verifies the fixture/application pipeline; it measures neither model quality nor generalization. No live provider observations were collected.", "",

See request-evidence.json and README.md.", "",
        "## Procedure and observed results", "",
        "Run `uv run python -m intake.demo`, then `uv run python -m intake.evaluate .artifacts/accuracy/extractions.jsonl`. The demo exports only the 20 supplied documents to deliverables. Its separate evaluation export includes the synthetic request. Both pass through the same provider interface, validator, routing and durable queue.", "",
        f"Observed: {result['scalar_matches']}/{result['scalar_denominator']} exact scalar matches (12 fields × 21 messages); {result['routing_matches']}/{result['routing_denominator']} exact routing matches (status, owner, next_action × 21). Null matches: {result['null_matches']}/{result['null_denominator']}. Factual errors: {len(result['factual_errors'])}; comparison failures: {len(result['failures'])}. Every response source is mock.", "",
        "Equality is exact JSON/Python value equality, including case/punctuation, with no fuzzy matching. Every scalar slot counts, including absent fields on withdrawals/other requests: an expected null matches only a successfully extracted null. An error, missing document or wholly null extraction scores zero for all 12 slots, including expected nulls. No inapplicable slots are removed. Routing is scored separately. Duplicate current IDs fail evaluation; unexpected IDs are reported and fail the command.", "",
        "A wrong non-null scalar is reported as a factual error; omitted expected facts are comparison failures. Purpose excerpts have exact source-derived targets, so a different truthful excerpt still fails exact match and requires human adjudication. This conservative rule is not a semantic truth metric. supporting_quotes and issues are excluded from scalar accuracy; validation checks schema, exact quote substrings, scalar evidence coverage, ISO dates and missing-fact issue coverage. Targeted tests inspect conflict/correction, relative-date, mismatch and override behavior. These do not prove all possible language conflicts were detected.", "",
        "## Independently expected fields", "",
        "null means absent or unresolved. Every request_date is explicit in the message; export timestamps supply no business facts.", "",
    ]
    golds = expected()
    for columns in [
        ["document_id", "request_id", "request_date", "kind", "requester", "team", "manager"],
        ["document_id", "system", "environment", "permission", "start_date", "end_date"],
        ["document_id", "business_purpose"],
    ]:

        for gold in golds:

                                          for c in columns) + " |")
        lines.append("")
    lines += ["## Expected routing and reasons", "",
              "| Document | Status | Owner | Next action |", "| --- | --- | --- | --- |"]
    for gold in golds:
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join([gold["document_id"], *ROUTES[gold["route"]]]) + " |")
    lines += [
        "", "IT-003 lacks environment/permission and explicit dates. IT-004 contradicts environments without correction. IT-005 is a withdrawal; rule 2 allows missing access facts. Complete staging/read requests use System Owner; complete production/write/admin requests use Security Review. No result grants approval.", "",

        "fixtures/synthetic/SYN-001.json rephrases IT-001 using different sentence order and window wording. Its source text is:", "",
        "> " + json.loads((ROOT / "fixtures/synthetic/SYN-001.json").read_text())["message"], "",
        "Its expected fields were written explicitly in the TSV; its mock fixture explicitly replays the paraphrase. It participates in every denominator above. Fresh wording has not been tested against a live model. To evaluate live results, use a separate database, intake both source directories with --provider openai, run workers, export separately, and run intake.evaluate on that export. Inspect each mismatch, issue and quote manually before claiming factual accuracy.", "",
    ]

    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

entire checkpoint list — List checkpoints on the current branch
List checkpoints on the current branch.

By default shows condensed checkpoints from the checkpoints branch for the
current branch. Use --pending for work that is not a checkpoint yet:

  - A preview of the next checkpoint for each session in this worktree with
    pending work. Agent turns are recorded in session state, not in git, so
    this work has no checkpoint ID until you commit it. The preview shows the
    turns since the last checkpoint, the files touched, subagent task records,
    and the prompts since the last checkpoint.
  - Subagent task records of other sessions on HEAD (not yet condensed).
  - Logs-only resume points recovered from commits whose logs are already
    condensed.

Use --outgoing to see what your next 'git push' sends: the checkpoints
queued for the checkpoint sync remote, read from local state with no network
call. Each one shows its ID, age, agent, first prompt (or summary) and the
files it touched. It needs the git-refs checkpoint backend, which pushes one
ref per checkpoint; the git-branch backend pushes entire/checkpoints/v1 as one
branch, so --outgoing reports an error there.

Output modes:
  --json              Machine-readable JSON instead of the human view.
  --pending           Select the pending dataset described above.
  --pending --json    The pending dataset as a JSON array.
  --outgoing          Select the outgoing dataset described above.
  --outgoing --json   The outgoing dataset as one JSON object.

Each --pending --json element has id, message, metadata_dir, date (RFC3339),
is_task_checkpoint, is_logs_only, and when set tool_use_id, condensation_id,
session_id and session_prompt. A next-checkpoint preview element has an empty
id, "is_next_checkpoint": true, and a "next_checkpoint" object:

  {"agent": "...", "turns": 2,
   "files_touched": ["..."],
   "task_records": [{"tool_use_id": "...", "subagent_type": "...",
                     "description": "...", "status": "running|completed"}],
   "prompts": ["..."]}

The arrays are always present, possibly empty.

The --outgoing --json object has checkpoint_push_disabled,
checkpoint_sync_remote, checkpoint_sync_remote_source and
checkpoint_sync_error (as in 'entire status --json'), stale_queue_entries
and a checkpoints array of {checkpoint_id, ref, created_at, agent,
session_count, prompt, summary, files_touched, error}. The array is always
present, possibly empty.

Optionally filter condensed checkpoints by session ID with --session
(not applicable with --pending or --outgoing).

+# Verification record
+
+Observed on 2026-11-08 using Python 3.12.3, uv 0.13.7, SQLite (Python sqlite3), and PostgreSQL 16 in a temporary Docker container. All extraction observations below used the deterministic mock. No live provider request, credential validation, or model-quality measurement was performed.
+
+## Commands and observed outcomes
+
+From the repository root, after installing the locked environment:
+
+```sh
+uv sync --locked
+.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
+.venv/bin/ruff check .
+.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q intake tests
+.venv/bin/python -m intake.demo
+.venv/bin/python -m intake.evaluate .artifacts/accuracy/extractions.jsonl
+git diff --check
+```
+
+The dependency environment was created successfully by uv. SQLite tests: **48 passed**. Ruff: **All checks passed**. Compilation and diff whitespace checks completed successfully. The report generator exported 20 current mock records and a linked 20-entry queue. Its separate evaluation export contained the 20 supplied documents plus the authored synthetic paraphrase. Observed comparison: **252/252 scalar fields**, including **21/21 expected nulls**, and **63/63 routing fields**; no comparison failures, factual errors or unexpected documents. These are fixture replay observations, not live-model accuracy. Full comparison rules and all independently authored expectations are in accuracy.md and tests/expected.tsv.
+
+The shared-database test command was:
+
+```sh
+TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/postgres \
+  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -x --tb=short
+```
+
+Observed on the dedicated temporary PostgreSQL 16 database: **48 passed**. Each test used a uniquely named schema and removed that schema afterward. The local test instance used a localhost-only port and temporary trust authentication; this is a test setup, not the recommended shared-service authentication configuration. The test container was stopped after verification. The same suite runs against SQLite when TEST_DATABASE_URL is absent.
+
+The documented CLI sequence `init`, `intake materials/requests`, and `work --drain` also ran successfully. The report generator uses fresh temporary storage and invokes the real export command. The subprocess tests exercise the CLI independently of the test process.
+
+## Assertions and intended comparisons
+
+| Check | Assertion and intended comparison | Observation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Complete request | IT-001 facts agree with message; hash equals SHA-256 of original bytes; route System Owner | Passed |
+| Source-derived dataset | Independently authored TSV expectations versus 12 extracted scalars and three routing fields for all 21 messages | Passed, 252 + 63 matches |
+| Missing facts / relative dates | Null fields retained; clarification wins over risk routing when required facts absent | Passed |
+| Conflicts / corrections | IT-004 environment and IT-020 manager unresolved; IT-008 environment and IT-015 dates use explicit corrections | Passed |
+| Withdrawal / identifier | Withdrawal routes under rule 2; IT-016 document keeps IT-061 request ID and mismatch issue | Passed |
+| Embedded instructions | Legitimate IT-006 read permission remains; override quoted and issue recorded; inspect-message takes precedence | Passed |
+| Provider completion | Refusal, failed/incomplete response, interrupted message, malformed JSON and missing output never become successful extractions | Passed with substituted provider/HTTP responses |
+| Provider transport | Request body/schema/timeout/auth-header plumbing; HTTP 429/503 versus 400/401; timeout and missing API_KEY; private error text omitted | Passed using synthetic transports and placeholder credential only |
+| Validation | Schema errors, fabricated quotes, invalid dates and empty values rejected; source fact coverage required | Passed |
